summary_own_words: General prohibition on agreements or collusion about production, supply, distribution, storage or acquisition of goods/services that harm competition.
Lists practices presumed to harm competition (e.g., price fixing, output limits, market sharing, bid rigging).
Addresses tie-in, exclusive supply, exclusive distribution, refusal to deal and resale price maintenance arrangements.
Carves out certain acts from the prohibition (read text for exact scope).
Prohibits abuse of dominance; s.16(2) lists presumed abuses (e.g., unfair/discriminatory pricing, predatory pricing below cost, limiting production or access).
Commission's pre-inquiry and inquiry procedure on complaints or its own initiative.
Interim orders to stop conduct that appears to breach ss.15-16 during the process.
Financial penalties; secondary sources cite up to 10% of average turnover (3 years) or up to three times profit for cartel conduct. Confirm against text.
Sources conflict on whether s.21 covers combinations or agreements made outside Bangladesh. MUST check the text before citing.
Establishes the Bangladesh Competition Commission.
Elements of a valid contract: free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and object.
Defines free consent; consent induced by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake is not free.
Contracts obtained through dominant position over the other party's will.
Consideration or object is unlawful if forbidden by law, defeats law, is fraudulent or opposed to public policy.
Agreements restraining a lawful profession, trade or business are void (limited exception for sale of goodwill). Key hook for non-competes and exclusivity.
Agreements restricting enforcement of rights through ordinary legal proceedings are void to that extent (arbitration carve-out).
Compensation for loss naturally arising from breach; no remote or indirect loss.
Where a sum is named for breach, courts award reasonable compensation not exceeding the named amount.
Defines contract of indemnity (relevant to liability allocation clauses).
Implied conditions/warranties on title, description, quality/fitness and sample.
Express terms can negate or vary implied terms (check exact wording).
Prohibits contracts, combinations and conspiracies in restraint of trade; criminal and civil enforcement.
Prohibits monopolization, attempts and conspiracies to monopolize.
Unlawful to sell/lease goods on condition of not dealing with competitors where effect may substantially lessen competition or tend to create monopoly.
Private right of action with threefold damages and attorney's fees.
Prohibits acquisitions that may substantially lessen competition.
Restricts price discrimination between competing purchasers of like goods with competitive injury.
Declares unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts unlawful.
Court may refuse to enforce unconscionable contracts or clauses.
Contractual limits on remedies and consequential damages allowed unless unconscionable or remedy fails of essential purpose.
Rules for excluding or modifying implied warranties (conspicuousness etc.).
Liquidated damages valid only if reasonable in light of anticipated or actual harm.
Good-faith duties in requirements/output contracts; exclusive dealing implies best efforts.
Prohibits agreements, decisions and concerted practices that restrict competition and affect trade between Member States.
Prohibited agreements are automatically void.
Conditions for exemption (efficiencies, consumer benefit, indispensability, no elimination of competition).
Prohibits abuse of a dominant position (unfair prices, limiting production, discrimination, tying).
Resale price maintenance and certain territorial/customer restrictions remove block-exemption benefit.
Non-compete obligations exceeding five years or post-term non-competes are not exempted (limited exceptions).
Fines up to 10% of total turnover for infringements of Arts. 101-102.
Concentrations that significantly impede effective competition are incompatible with the internal market.
Defines fundamental terms: proposal, acceptance, promise, consideration, agreement, reciprocal promises, void agreements, and enforceable contracts.
Parties must be of the age of majority according to the law to which they are subject, sound mind, and not disqualified from contracting by any law.
Coercion is committing or threatening to commit any act forbidden by the Penal Code, or unlawful detaining of property to compel consent.
Fraud includes suggestion as a fact of that which is not true, active concealment, promise made without intention to perform, or deceptive acts to induce contract.
Positive assertion not warranted by information, breach of duty causing mistake, or causing a party to make mistake as to substance of contract subject matter.

topic: voidability of agreements without free consent
summary_own_words: Agreements caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation are voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
Agreement void where both parties are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement.

topic: agreements void if consideration unlawful in part
summary_own_words: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one of any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, agreement is void.
Agreement made without consideration is void unless expressed in writing and registered, or made on account of natural love and affection, or promise to compensate past voluntary services.
Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void.

topic: obligation of parties to perform contracts
summary_own_words: Parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless performance is dispensed with or excused.
When a party promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, and fails to do so, contract becomes voidable at option of promisee if intention was that time should be of essence.
Agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract to do an act which becomes impossible or unlawful after contracting becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.

topic: effect of novation, rescission, and alteration
summary_own_words: If parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, original contract need not be performed.
Promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, performance of promise, or extend time, or accept any satisfaction.

topic: obligation to restore advantage under void agreement
summary_own_words: When an agreement is discovered to be void, or contract becomes void, person who received advantage is bound to restore it or compensate.
Indemnity-holder acting within authority can recover damages, costs of defense, and sums paid under compromise.
Defines contract of guarantee to perform promise, or discharge liability, of a third person in case of default. Parties: surety, principal debtor, creditor.
Liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless otherwise provided by the contract.

topic: discharge of surety by variance in terms
summary_own_words: Any variance made without surety's consent in terms of contract between principal debtor and creditor discharges surety as to transactions subsequent to variance.
Defines agreement, enterprise, cartel, turnover, dominant position, goods, market, predatory price, and vertical arrangements.
The Commission has power to inquire into agreements, dominant abuse or combinations taking place outside Bangladesh if they have an appreciable adverse effect on competition within Bangladesh.

topic: powers and functions of Competition Commission
summary_own_words: Commission is empowered to eliminate anti-competitive practices, promote and sustain competition, protect consumer interests, and ensure freedom of trade.

Presumed abuses include unfair/discriminatory pricing, predatory pricing below production cost, limiting technical development, denying market access, or making contract conclusion subject to supplementary obligations.
Any person aggrieved by an order or decision of the Bangladesh Competition Commission may appeal to the High Court Division within 60 days.
Contract of sale of goods is a contract whereby seller transfers or agrees to transfer property in goods to buyer for price. Agreement to sell becomes sale when time elapses or conditions fulfilled.
Condition is a stipulation essential to main purpose of contract, breach of which gives right to treat contract as repudiated. Warranty is collateral, giving right to claim damages only.

topic: implied condition as to title and quiet possession
summary_own_words: Implied condition that seller has right to sell goods, and implied warranty that buyer shall have and enjoy quiet possession free from undisclosed third-party encumbrances.

topic: implied condition of merchantable quality and fitness
summary_own_words: Implied condition that goods shall be reasonably fit for purpose disclosed to seller where buyer relies on seller's skill, and of merchantable quality where goods bought by description.

topic: sale by person not the owner
summary_own_words: Nemo dat quod non habet principle: buyer acquires no better title than seller had, unless owner is precluded by conduct or sale is by mercantile agent in ordinary course of business.
Where property in goods has passed to buyer and buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay, seller may sue for price of goods.
Where buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to accept and pay for goods, seller may sue for damages for non-acceptance measured by natural and direct loss.
Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, no judicial authority shall intervene in matters governed by the Act except as specifically provided.
Arbitration agreement must be in writing (document signed by parties, exchange of letters, telex, telegrams, emails, or claim/defense admissions).

topic: stay of legal proceedings for arbitration
summary_own_words: Court must refer parties to arbitration upon application by a party to an arbitration agreement before filing written statement on the substance of the dispute.
Court has power before or during arbitral proceedings to grant interim preservation, custody, or sale of goods, detention, or interim injunctions.
Arbitral tribunal may rule on its own jurisdiction, including ruling on any objections with respect to the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement.

topic: grounds for setting aside arbitral award
summary_own_words: High Court or District Court may set aside award only if party under incapacity, agreement invalid, lack of proper notice, dispute outside scope, or award in conflict with public policy of Bangladesh.
Where time for setting aside expired or application rejected, arbitral award shall be enforced under Code of Civil Procedure in the same manner as a decree of court.

topic: recognition and enforcement of foreign arbitral awards
summary_own_words: Foreign arbitral award made in a reciprocating New York Convention state shall be recognized as binding and enforceable in Bangladesh.
Specific performance enforceable when agreed act is unquantifiable in pecuniary damages, or when pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.

Contracts for the non-performance of which compensation in money is adequate relief, contracts running into minute details, contracts of personal service, and contracts revocable in nature cannot be specifically enforced.
Perpetual injunction granted to prevent breach of obligation where defendant invades plaintiff's rights and pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.

Where a contract comprises an affirmative agreement to do a certain act, coupled with a negative agreement not to do a certain act, court may grant injunction to perform negative agreement even if affirmative agreement cannot be specifically enforced.

topic: binding effect of memorandum and articles
summary_own_words: Memorandum and articles bind company and members as if signed and sealed by each member to observe all provisions.

topic: form and validity of company contracts
summary_own_words: Contracts on behalf of a company may be made in writing under common seal, or in writing signed by any person acting under express or implied authority.

topic: director disclosure of interest in contracts
summary_own_words: Every director interested in any contract or arrangement with company must disclose the nature of their interest at meeting of board of directors.
Members holding required shareholding may apply to High Court Division where company affairs are being conducted in a manner prejudicial to members or public interest.
No person in Bangladesh shall make any payment to or for the credit of any person resident outside Bangladesh without general or special permission of Bangladesh Bank.

topic: restrictions on foreign corporate control and technology royalties
summary_own_words: Regulates remittance of technical assistance fees, royalties, consultancy fees, and franchise fees to foreign principals subject to regulatory limits.
Employer may terminate employment of a permanent worker by giving 120 days notice for monthly rated workers (or wages in lieu) plus compensation of 30 days wages for every completed year of service.
Permanent worker may resign by giving 30 days notice to employer. Workers with 5+ years of continuous service are entitled to gratuity or separation compensation.
